Commentary.Commentary: That is it then from this game and now three teams have made it through to the Super 4s stage of the competition. With one spot remaining, Sri Lanka takes on Afghanistan in the final game of the initial stage in Group B. Afghanistan need to win to have a shot at making it through whereas Sri Lanka will be eyeing to consolidate the top spot in their group. That game will be played on September 5 at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore and will begin at 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT). Our build-up though will begin much sooner. Cheers!

India's skipper, Rohit Sharma is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his brilliant knock. He says that, to be honest, there were nerves to start with but is glad to have stayed on and found his form. Adds that the flick he played was meant to go someplace else but the timing was much better than he thought. On India's team selection for the World Cup, he says that they knew the Asia Cup wouldn't give them the whole picture of what the team would look like for the mega event and adds that they didn't play their best cricket in these two games but the guys are starting to come good and they need to keep ticking all boxes. Mentions that they did well to recover with the bat in the last game and the bowling was decent in this game but the fielding and catching certainly need to improve.
The Presentation ceremony...

Nepal's skipper Rohit Paudel says that the openers did a very good job for them. Adds that the middle order could have done better. Reckons that they were 30–40 runs short. Feels that had the middle order done well, they could have scored 260–270. Mentions that their lower order has done a great job in the last few months. States that it was hard to bowl in these conditions but feels that the bowlers did well.

Shubman Gill is in for a chat. He says that he definitely enjoyed the knock. Adds that it was disappointing the way he got out against Pakistan and wanted to finish the game here. Mentions that Rohit Sharma is the kind of player who wants to take on the bowlers aerially while he wants to go for the boundaries and that works well for them. Reckons that Nepal bowled very well with the new ball. Shares that they knew it would be easier to bat, once the ball got wet in the outfield.

Nepal are out of the Asia Cup but they will take a lot of positives from this game. After a tentative start with the bat, the opening pair of Aasif Sheikh and Kushal Bhurtel started attacking with the latter finding the fence with ease. Right at the end of the first Powerplay, Bhurtel fell and that triggered a mini-collapse. Sheikh though remained resolute and along with Gulsan Jha stitched a steady stand notching up a half-century in the process as well. It was then another solid stand between Dipendra Singh Airee and Sompal Kami that took Nepal to well over the 200-run mark. With the ball, Karan KC started brilliantly and troubled the Indian skipper in the first over but that was the best it got as they were put to the sword once play resumed after the rain break.

INDIA ARE THROUGH TO THE SUPER FOURS! Finally, we got a game in and we got a result as well. India have made short work of the revised target set by Nepal and have cruised into the Super 4s. But it wasn't all light work with all the rain around and the grit shown by the Nepal batters in the first half of the game. India dropped 3 catches very early and then it was Ravindra Jadeja who bailed them out with some quick wickets and ended up with three in total. The pacers were a bit too short for the most part but did get the job done in the latter part as Mohammed Siraj too picked up three wickets. Coming to the chase, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill had to wait a long time due to the rain but once play resumed both were aggressive and just ripped apart the Nepal bowlers to clinch a brilliant 10-wicket win.

FOUR! THAT'S IT! Jha drifts on the pads, on a full length, Shubman Gill gets inside the line and helps it past short fine leg for a boundary. India win by 10 wickets and they are through to the Super Four!

Commentary.Commentary: This one comes in with the arm and is bowled around middle, Shubman Gill defends it out with soft hands.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up outside off, Shubman Gill pushes it out to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Lalit Rajbanshi to Shubman Gill, No run.

Nicely bowled! Perfect length around off and seaming away really late. Rohit Sharma's feet go nowhere as he pokes at it and the ball zips past the outside edge.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and in the channel, Rohit Sharma stands tall and eases it toward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and straight, Rohit Sharma looks for the flick again but has to adjust and defend it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, tapped away in front of cover-point for a quick run by Shubman Gill.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Karan KC to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fullish length around off and angling in, Rohit Sharma with a slight shimmie across and he flicks it past square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: After a long wait, we are all set to resume. The two umpires and the Nepal players make their way out to the middle. They are followed by two Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill. Karan KC has the ball in hand and will complete his over. Here we go...

UPDATE - 10.05 pm (4.35 pm GMT) - Great news! Play will restart at 10.15 pm IST (4.45 pm GMT). It will be a 23-over game with 5 overs of the first Powerplay. The revised target for India is 145. Folks, don't go anywhere as we have a match on our hands here.

UPDATE - 9.37 pm (4.07 pm GMT) - Another big update coming from the ground now as the two umpires are in conversation with one of the broadcaster's commentators. The umpires say that the mop-up work might begin by 10 pm IST (4.30 pm GMT) and the play must start by 10.20 pm IST for a 20-over game to constitute. They also say that the closing time is somewhere around 11.36 pm IST (5.06 pm GMT). Stick around as we should have a final verdict on the future of this game in some time.

UPDATE - 9.23 pm IST (3.53 pm GMT) - Some positive news! It has stopped raining and the ground staff are already out there to remove the water from the covers before taking them off. The cut-off time for a 20-over chase is 10.20 pm IST (4.50 pm GMT). There is still hope but it all depends on how much time it takes for the ground staff to dry up the outfield. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 8.49 pm IST (3.19 pm GMT) - The intensity of rain has reduced but it is still a steady drizzle in Pallekele. The rain needs to completely stop for the ground staff to begin removing the covers. Considering that it was bucketing down, it would take some time for them to get the field ready to play. Having had a long delay during the Nepal Innings as well, we will start losing overs soon. Stick around for more news.

UPDATE - 8.19 pm IST (2.49 pm GMT) - Uh oh, not again! The umpires have had enough of the persistent drizzle and they have asked the ground staff to bring the covers on. The rain gods have not been kind on what has been a frustrating day so far. As we say, the rain has gotten heavier, meaning the entire ground will have to be covered now. To add to everyone's misery, there is not much wind blowing across to blow the rain away. All we can do right now is hope that the rain subsides for us to resume soon. Stay tuned for further updates.
FOUR! That'll release the pressure nicely and Rohit Sharma is off the mark. Pitched up on the stumps, Sharma makes up his mid early and lofts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A lovely delivery to end the over. Hard length on off and this one seams away off the deck, Shubman Gill looks to come forward and play at it but is beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Sompal Kami to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Timed to perfection yet again by Shubman Gill. Another short one from Sompal Kami outside off, Gill gets on top of the bounce and forehand-slaps it in front of square on the off side for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Sompal Kami to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Good length around off, Shubman Gill blocks it off the front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Sompal Kami to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much better from Sompal Kami! Bowls it a lot fuller and outside off, getting it to swing away a long way and late as well. Gill looks to play at it but is beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Sompal Kami to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Sompal Kami to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, what timing! Good length, slightly shorter and outside off, moving away as well. Shubman Gill stands tall and punches it gently on the up as the ball rockets through the cover region for a boundary. Gill is up and running!

Commentary.Commentary: Sompal Kami will steam in from the other end.
Excellent first over barring the wide first up from Karan KC. Slightly shorter over middle, Rohit Sharma tries to come out of his crease and nudges it toward mid-wicket
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: An absolute jaffa! Perfect length on a tight line around off and this one straightens off the deck. Rohit Sharma looks to block but the ball zips past the outside edge into the clutches of the keeper. The bowler thinks there's an edge but the umpire turns it down. The replays do confirm that there was no edge on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: And again! Seems to be going down again and Rohit Sharma is really struggling out there. Length ball around middle, angling in, Sharma looks to get forward and flick but falls over a bit and misses again, getting hit on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A big, big appeal for LBW but the umpire says no. It sure did look close and Nepal have taken the review. Karan KC pitches this one right up on off stump and gets the ball to nip back in. There is clear daylight between the bat and the ball and Ball Tracking shows that the ball is missing leg stump. Review lost as well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and angling into off, Rohit Sharma plays it out to mid on.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Starts off with a loosener. Karan KC bowls this one on a fullish length and around the pads, angling down leg. Wide signalled by the umpire.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Karan KC to Rohit Sharma, Wide!
